content:
Elliot Price: Hey folks — doing final doc pass for unit econ dashboard. Need quick alignment on naming conventions before I update Confluence ADR + the backfill/reconciliation runbooks.

Elliot Price: Specifically: what’s the canonical metric name for the headline KPI? I’ve seen `blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens`, `blended_cost_usd_per_1m_output_tokens`, and `blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens_usd` across drafts.

Logan Wright: +1. In the semantic layer we standardized on `*_usd_*` pattern to avoid unit ambiguity. I’d vote `blended_cost_usd_per_1m_output_tokens`.

Nadia Rahman: Agree. Also please make sure it’s explicitly *output tokens* in denominator (generated/completion), not total tokens. We have a separate input token cost view.

Elliot Price: Got it. So headline = `blended_cost_usd_per_1m_output_tokens` and denominator is output-only.

Cole Summers: From reconciliation side: we also need to be consistent in docs about what “blended” includes.

Cole Summers: Proposed wording: compute (GPU time allocated), cache effects (effective cost after cache savings), + allocated overhead; excludes revenue-side discounts/credits unless explicitly switching to “net” view. Finance asked that “blended” be gross-cost aligned to COGS allocation, not pricing.

Rishi Malhotra: Yes. For FP&A, default should be gross cost (COGS-aligned). If there’s a “net” view later that applies credits/discounts, it must be labeled and access-restricted.

Marissa Cole: For Console, we’re using “Blended cost ($/1M output tokens)” as display name. Happy to map display name -> canonical field name in the glossary section.

Allison Grant: For SRE alerts we need the exact names too. In the observability pack PR we used `unit_econ_blended_cost_usd_per_1m_output_tokens` as the time series name. Can docs note the mapping?

Elliot Price: Yep. I’ll add a section: “Canonical metric field names (semantic layer) vs dashboard display labels vs alert series names”.

Aisha Bello: Also please put the freshness SLO names in the doc exactly as used by alerts.

Aisha Bello: Ex: `unit_econ_daily_partition_freshness_minutes` + `unit_econ_reconciliation_variance_pct`. People keep asking what alert corresponds to what check.

Logan Wright: Re: cache metrics — we’ve got 2 rates now:
- `prefix_cache_hit_rate` (fraction of requests with prefix cache hits)
- `kv_cache_hit_rate` (token-level KV reuse rate)

Logan Wright: And an attribution field `cache_savings_usd` (estimated) that rolls into blended cost.

Nadia Rahman: Minor correction: kv cache hit is not literally “hit rate” in the HTTP sense; it’s computed from token accounting. But naming is fine as long as docs say “derived estimate.”

Elliot Price: Cool. I’ll include caveat: “cache_savings_usd is an estimate from token-level accounting; not a billable line item.”

Cole Summers: Please also call out reconciliation tolerance + lateness behavior:
- we exclude last ~N hours of partitions from reconciliation job by default (late metering events)
- expected variance <= 0.5% daily; alert at 1.0% (unless Finance changes)

Rishi Malhotra: Confirming: 0.5% expected, 1.0% page/notify is fine.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: (reaction)

Marissa Cole: What about dimensions naming? In UI filters we show “Tier”, “Region”, “Model”, “Quant profile”. Under the hood we should align to:
- `customer_tier` (self_serve/dedicated/private/enterprise)
- `cloud_region`
- `model_id` + `model_family`
- `quantization_profile`
- `runtime_config` (optional)

Logan Wright: +1. Please do not use `tier` alone in docs; we’ve got other “tiers” in billing.

Elliot Price: Noted. I’ll standardize on `customer_tier` and list allowed values.

Elliot Price: Confluence updates I’m planning:
1) ADR-0142: definition + exclusions + reconciliation strategy (link)
2) Runbook: backfill + reprocessing partitions + validation checklist (link)
3) Add a short “Metric glossary / naming conventions” section to both.

Elliot Price: Can someone sanity-check the exact ADR title? I have “ADR-0142 Blended cost per 1M output tokens (definition)”.

Cole Summers: That matches what I’ve been referencing. Just ensure the metric name string appears exactly once in the “Canonical name” line.

Nadia Rahman: Also: use “output tokens” not “completion tokens” in public-facing-ish docs. Internally we used completion sometimes, but it confuses with chat vs text endpoints.

Elliot Price: Will do. I’ll add a note: “output tokens == generated tokens (completion tokens) across chat/text routes”.

Aisha Bello: Last thing: include owners at the bottom of doc. For alerts/runbooks:
- Pipeline owner: Nadia
- Reconciliation owner: Cole
- SLO/alerts: me + Allison

Allison Grant: Yep.

Logan Wright: Data contracts page also needs the canonical names, but that’s separate doc. Elliot, if you update ADR + runbook today, I’ll update data contracts tomorrow to match.

Elliot Price: Perfect. I’ll post links here once merged. Targeting EOD.

Elliot Price: Action items:
- [Elliot] update ADR + runbook with canonical names + glossary
- [Logan] follow-up update to data contracts page (naming alignment)
- [Aisha/Allison] confirm alert series names match glossary

Marissa Cole: Thanks. Once you paste links I’ll drop them into the Console PR description so reviewers stop bikeshedding the naming.

Elliot Price: :white_check_mark: will do.
